headline: Highest risk is medium data leakage: Mentat reads/writes files and uses a model provider, while whisper is file-based and local-only, so shared-workspace exposure is plausible but not directly evidenced.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Mentat can read and write filesystem content and uses stdin/stdout plus model-provider calls; whisper only consumes audio files and has no interactive tool surface. There is no documented shared channel or parser bridge between them, so prompt injection is limited to unusual manual file handoff rather than a default pathway.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies whisper-transcribed text into files that Mentat later edits as instructions, injection becomes possible.
IF both agents are pointed at the same shared text workspace, Mentat may treat attacker-controlled content as guidance.
mitigations: Keep whisper outputs in a separate directory from Mentat inputs.
Require a human review step before Mentat acts on any transcribed text.
Use explicit instruction delimiters in files passed between tools.
Disable automatic ingestion of generated transcripts into task prompts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Mentat reads selected files, writes diffs, and sends prompts to a configured model provider; whisper reads audio files and is local-only with no network egress. A shared filesystem can expose audio or code across the pair, and Mentat's provider calls can transmit whatever it ingests, so leakage is plausible in default workspace setups.
conditions: IF audio files and source files are stored in the same workspace, Mentat can access content adjacent to whisper inputs.
IF Mentat is configured with sensitive files selected on the command line, those contents may be sent to its model provider.
mitigations: Separate audio and code into different directories.
Restrict Mentat to a minimal file list per task.
Avoid placing secrets in any directory Mentat scans.
Confirm provider-side retention settings before processing sensitive files.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Mentat can write the filesystem and modify git state, while whisper cannot write files, modify git, or use multiple instances. The pair therefore has little direct write-write contention; the main overlap is Mentat's filesystem access, which whisper lacks, so conflict risk is small.
conditions: IF an operator wraps whisper in a separate script that writes into the same git tree, Mentat and that wrapper can contend on files.
IF Mentat is run concurrently with another writer outside this profile, git conflicts may occur.
mitigations: Run Mentat on a branch with short-lived commits.
Serialize any external file writers before Mentat edits.
Keep whisper outputs outside the git working tree until review.
Use per-task output directories.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Mentat produces diff-based edit proposals and whisper produces audio-to-text outputs, but whisper does not act on Mentat's results and has no downstream authority. Without a documented pipeline where one agent's output is automatically trusted by the other, cascading error is limited to manual misuse rather than a default failure mode.
conditions: IF a human feeds whisper transcripts directly into Mentat without verification, transcription errors can propagate into edits.
IF Mentat-generated text is reused as ground truth for later transcription tasks, errors can cascade across work products.
mitigations: Verify transcripts before using them as edit instructions.
Require a second reviewer for any Mentat diff derived from whisper output.
Keep source audio and edited code in separate task queues.
Mark machine-generated text clearly in filenames or headers.

E_compliance.rationale: Both agents are open-source and docs-only, and neither profile shows regulated-data handling or residency constraints. The only concrete compliance issue is that Mentat handles model-provider API keys and may send selected file contents to a provider, while whisper is local-only; no cross-border or certification mismatch is documented, so risk stays low.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed in files selected for Mentat, provider-side processing may create a policy mismatch.
IF an operator requires local-only processing for audio, whisper satisfies that but Mentat may not.
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from Mentat inputs.
Review provider terms and retention settings.
Document which files may be sent off-device.
Use local-only workflows for sensitive audio when possible.
